title: Stadium Tours: A Family Day Out for Sports Fans
description: Stadium tours for sports-mad kids and teens: what you see behind the scenes, booking tips, match-day restrictions and combining a tour with the club museum.
h1: Stadium tours for sports-mad kids and teens
intro: Sit in the dugout, walk the players’ tunnel and see the trophies up close. Stadium tours are a dream day out for young football, rugby and cricket fans.

image.alt: A family walking along a wooden boardwalk through a field at golden hour

cardText: Dugouts, tunnels and trophies: how stadium tours work.

blocks.title: Scout’s stadium tip
blocks.text: Tours don’t usually run on match days, and dates change when fixtures move. Book a weekday in the school holidays and double-check the day before.
points: Many tours include the club museum
A tour voucher makes a great gift

sections.html: Tours vary, but often include the dressing rooms, the players’ tunnel, the pitchside dugouts, the press room and the trophy cabinet, with a guide sharing stories. Many big clubs and national stadiums run regular tours.

• Book online. Popular slots sell out in the holidays.
  • Check for match-day and event closures.
  • Ask about accessibility: some routes include lots of stairs.
A stadium tour makes a brilliant experience gift or birthday day out for a sports-mad teen. See behind-the-scenes tours for more.

faqs.q: Do stadium tours run on match days?
faqs.a: Usually not. Tours are often cancelled or limited on match and event days, so check the schedule before booking.
